requirements.evidence: All contract classes present: CreateQueue (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:17 trims, slugifies default/explicit slug, is_active true, pre-check + QueryException->ValidationException at :50-58), UpdateQueue with named nullable params and whereKeyNot self-slug check (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:16,79-86), SetQueueAccess upsert/delete with audit logs and no revoke log when nothing deleted (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:45-65), QueuePermission enum, QueueAccess model/factory, migration with cascades + unique pair (migration:16-21), QueuePolicy create/update/manageAccess/call incl. is_array guard (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:72-75). CallNextTicket authorizes after active check (CallNextTicket.php:32); Ticket::call locks queue, checks active, authorizes, then waiting check (Ticket.php:96-109). Gaps: isUniqueViolation only matches SQLSTATE 23000 or the strings 'UNIQUE'/'Duplicate', so a Postgres race (23505, 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint') would still surface as a raw QueryException; Ticket::call locks ticket then queue while CallNextTicket locks queue first (lock-order inversion).

security.evidence: Every new action authorizes server-side (CreateQueue.php:19, UpdateQueue.php:18, SetQueueAccess.php:27); both call paths enforce `call` (CallNextTicket.php:32, Ticket.php:107); permissions validated as known strings (SetQueueAccess.php:29-35); corrupted non-array permissions deny. Small gaps: SetQueueAccess runs the cross-entity ValidationException check before authorization (:20-25), so a non-manager gets a validation error instead of AuthorizationException for mismatched pairs; SQLSTATE 23000 also matches FK/NOT NULL violations and would be reported as a duplicate slug.

Existing CallNextTicket tests were updated by adding owner memberships, not weakened. Missing: the DB-unique race path, an other-entity manager in UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess auth tests, Ticket::call by a granted employee; filler assertions like `expect($entity->id)->not->toBeNull()` add noise.

scope.evidence: All changed files serve the task: actions, enum, model, factory, migration, policy, two call paths, docs, CHANGELOG and tests; CallNextTicketTest edits only add the owner membership needed by the new authorization. No UI, no delete action.

issues.explanation: Unique-violation detection only recognises SQLSTATE 23000 or the case-sensitive strings 'UNIQUE'/'Duplicate', so on PostgreSQL (23505, lowercase message) a slug race would leak a raw QueryException, and on MySQL 23000 also misreports FK/NOT NULL errors as duplicate slugs.
Ticket::call locks the ticket row before the queue row while CallNextTicket locks the queue first, an inverted lock order that can deadlock under concurrent calls.
The cross-entity ValidationException is thrown before Gate authorization, so a non-manager probing mismatched membership/queue pairs gets a validation error rather than AuthorizationException.
Name/slug validation messages and the isUniqueViolation helper are copy-pasted between the two actions instead of being shared.
The DB-unique race path that must become a ValidationException is untested, and UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess authorization tests omit a manager of another entity.
Filler assertions like `expect($entity->id)->not->toBeNull()` exist only to use destructured variables and add noise.

review.summary: The change implements queue create/update, per-queue access grants with audit logging, a QueuePolicy, the queue_access migration/model/factory, and call authorization on both call paths, with docs, changelog and solid tests. Remaining problems: portability of the unique-violation detection, a lock-order inversion between the two call paths, and duplicated helpers. None of these block approval, so it is approved with nits.
